title: How a project actually runs
lede: Nine steps, from first inquiry to final invoice — no surprises in between.
timeline: Typical timeline: 3 weeks for a micro project, up to 9 weeks for a medium one.

inquiry.title: Inquiry
inquiry.description: You reach out with your project idea — through the contact form, however rough the idea still is.

discoveryCall.title: Discovery call
discoveryCall.description: We talk through goals, wishes, materials, and budget directly — no forms, just a conversation.

briefQuote.title: Design brief & quote
briefQuote.description: A written brief scoping what's in and out, with a quote structured as MVP plus optional extras, so you can scale the project to your budget.

deposit.title: Deposit (50%)
deposit.description: Due on accepting the offer — production begins as soon as the deposit lands.

concept.title: Concept phase
concept.description: First visual drafts of UI and gameplay, with a feedback round before we move forward.

gameplay.title: Gameplay construction
gameplay.description: A playable but non-final build, with a feedback round focused on mechanics.

polish.title: Final polish
polish.description: Feedback on a finished but not-yet-tested build — bugs may still show up at this stage, and that's expected.

qaDelivery.title: QA & delivery
qaDelivery.description: Testing on the devices and platforms agreed with you, then final delivery.

qa.title: QA, stated openly
qa.body: Standard QA covers phone, tablet, and desktop across Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari via BrowserStack — that covers the large majority of real-world bugs. QA isn't the studio's core specialty, and we say so upfront: if a project needs broader device or OS coverage, that's arranged through an external QA partner and scoped into the budget at the brief stage, not discovered as a surprise later.
qa.russel: We know our boundaries — and we've already got a plan for the edge cases.

ai.title: AI-assisted workflow, stated openly
ai.body: Modern AI-assisted tools are used selectively across concepting, art, and development — it's part of how a single-person studio delivers studio-level production without studio-level overhead or timelines. This is a deliberate production choice backed by 20+ years of non-AI craft, not a shortcut: the work can be delivered fully without these tools, and using them selectively is what keeps fixed pricing realistic while a human designer makes every real decision.
ai.russel: Yes, AI tools are part of the toolkit — and yes, a human (me and my human) is still doing the designing.

tools.title: Tools
tools.communication: Communication adapts to your own stack — MS Teams, Slack, email, whatever your team already uses — rather than imposing a fixed tool on you.

postDelivery.title: After delivery
postDelivery.body: Engagement normally ends at delivery. Game-breaking bugs found within 3 months post-launch are covered under the original contract at no extra cost, excluding issues caused by platform updates or external circumstances outside the studio's control. Hosting and ongoing live-ops support aren't standard, but can be scoped and added — worth raising at the discovery call so it's planned for, not left implicit.
